races.title: State Assembly, District 11
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Lori D Wilson
cands.bio: Democratic Assemblymember for California's 11th District since a April 2022 special election. Former Suisun City mayor (elected 2018) and councilmember (elected 2012). Finance and accounting professional for over 20 years, including director of finance for national homebuilders. Chaired the California Legislative Black Caucus and the Assembly Transportation Committee.

endorsements.text: Ballotpedia lists 2026 endorsements from the Democratic Party of California, the California Federation of Labor Unions (AFL-CIO), the California Teachers Association, the California Nurses Association, IUOE Local 3, Equality California and YIMBY Action.

cands.gaps: The pages we had did not show her stance on data centers, homestead property taxes, foreign or investor land buying, immigration or H-1B, policing, gun laws, abortion or school choice. The list of bills she sponsored did not load, so we could not tie any bill to these issues. Her 2022 survey answers were general (housing, mental health, quality of life) and give no firm position on growth limits or land protection. Her Ballotpedia profile says she did not complete the 2024 or 2026 candidate surveys. We found no documented controversies, foreign ties or land-use statements, but the pages we had were limited.

local.label: Roots 100: Ballotpedia lists her birthplace as Fresno, and her campaign site and 2022 candidate survey say she is a native Californian raised on the west side of Fresno.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Assemblymember since 2022; Suisun City mayor from 2018, councilmember from 2012 and vice-mayor for six years; over 20 years in accounting and finance, including Solano County auditor, chief accountant at Fair Housing Napa Valley and director of finance for national homebuilders.
qual.why: Prior legislative service and local elected office combine with a long finance and budget career, which fits writing law and the state budget. Committee seats and chairs were not counted.

cands.name: Jenny Leilani Callison
cands.bio: Army veteran (2002–2006) and mother of two. Holds a master's in public policy and administration from Sacramento State. Says she worked more than 14 years in the California Legislature, most recently as Chief Consultant to the Senate Military and Veterans Affairs Committee. Ran for Assembly District 11 in 2022 and 2026.

endorsements.text: Ballotpedia lists Reform California, The Morning Answer with Jennifer Horn, and several voter-guide recommendations (April's Common Sense Cali Voters, Based in Malibu, Elizabeth Barcohana's Lady with a Brain Voter Guide).

cands.gaps: We found no record of elected office, so there are no votes or official actions to report. Her stated positions on data centers, homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land buyers, immigration and H-1B, abortion and policing were not found in the pages reviewed. Her campaign site says gun rights must be protected "while ensuring responsible safety measures" but gives no specifics. Her legislative staff titles and years come from her own statements and could not be checked against an official employment record. No news coverage or controversies were found. Her exact birth city was not found.

local.label: Roots 100: Ballotpedia says she was born in California and graduated from Winters Joint Union High School. Her campaign site calls her a Winters native and Dixon resident, and she describes herself as a lifelong Californian apart from four years in the Army.
